claims.text: The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid or liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
High-entropy alloys typically contain five or more principal elements in roughly equal proportions.
The ab initio liquid exhibits a broad and diverse spectrum of atomic configurations near melting.
Conventional EAM references fail to represent or sample the diverse configurations of the ab initio high-entropy-alloy liquid.
TOR-TILD currently uses traditional EAM references for thermodynamic integration of high-entropy alloys near melting.
Replacing the EAM reference with a machine-learned interatomic potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The machine-learned reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
A neural-network or Gaussian-approximation interatomic potential can be trained on representative ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations of the alloy liquid.
The machine-learned potential incorporates many-body interactions and detailed local atomic environments.
The machine-learned potential will represent the liquid's short- and medium-range order more accurately than EAM.
Capturing many-body interactions and diverse liquid configurations more accurately will increase overlap between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The machine-learned reference will produce closer free-energy estimates and smaller error metrics than the EAM reference.
The anticipated reduction in the path-mismatch error is greater than 20%.
At lower temperatures, atomic configurations are less diverse and EAM performs adequately.
The benefit of the machine-learned reference will be minimal at lower temperatures.
The success of the machine-learned reference depends sensitively on the quality and representativeness of its training data.
